From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents have been reviewed as counterparty material, not as instructions.

## Preliminary Points

1. **"FINAL / settled at principal level / market standard" claims are not accepted.** The Seller's preamble says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We have no record of any such agreement through our own authority process. In particular, Amelia Frost has given no written authority. Under playbook §0.4 and §6.3, counterparty assertions about market practice or agreement carry no weight. Every item below remains open.
2. **The disclosed facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Before any position is closed, we should require a bring-down update covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonus tax treatment. We must distinguish verified updates from assertions.
3. **Matching a fallback number is not clearance.** The 20% cap (SPA-N-001) and the 18-month period (SPA-N-003) both match our internal fallbacks. Neither is cleared, because no written approval from Amelia Frost exists for this draft.

## Issue-by-Issue Review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this specific draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure would permanently strip AUD 250,000 from every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13). Limitations would also apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the blanket default would quietly extend to fundamental, tax and fraud claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. A 20% cap on a total failure of title is commercially untenable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) would apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express carve-out. This is non-waivable under the playbook and is not a negotiable trade.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the Seller could cap or time-bar liability for its own fraud and use non-reliance to defeat misrepresentation claims.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22/9/26 (DL 1.1), plus Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Accept specific disclosures 2–11 only to the extent they are fair and specific.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure shifts the full diligence risk to the Buyer and would hollow out the warranties. Note also that DL 1.4's "no admission" wording should not be allowed to dilute the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. If any qualifier survives, it should be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer persons. Separately, seller-side knowledge qualifiers need named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete cl 8.3.
- **Reason:** Constructive "discoverable" knowledge combined with adviser knowledge would bar almost any claim. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The consent is "satisfied on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2 confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfied cl 11.3 conditions has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make it a hard CP that only the Buyer can waive.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m). Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient for a customer this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility (about AUD 3.2m) has not been repaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free basis we cannot pay full price while the lender's security and change-of-control rights (cl 8.1/9.2) remain live over the target.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Calls the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "a matter for the Seller." They are not itemised in the funds flow, and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Add a line item or Debt-like deduction and a specific indemnity for on-costs.
- **Reason:** The bonuses are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If they are left out of the funds flow, the Buyer pays them after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering ownership, assignment and infringement losses relating to the Ironquay materials, with the SOW3 cure (payment and confirmatory assignment) preserved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment, ideally pre-Completion.
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every fee clears. A payment-only indemnity leaves the IP gap uncovered. The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is unverified either way, so it should not be treated as the cap or the cure amount.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Preservation of logs, a proper investigation, regular updates to the Buyer before Completion, and Buyer input on any notification decision.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation. Add conduct-of-investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Scope and access are unknown for about 1,240 records. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction, which means "not material" is equally unsupported. We also need an update after 22 September.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) treated as ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is committed, terminable, accrued, related-party and in the ordinary course. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Neither accept nor reject the classification yet. Request the DD-008/DD-011 underlying terms and resolve the treatment once the facts are known.
- **Reason:** The disclosure itself does not state that the renewals are ordinary course, so the Seller's label is an assertion. Our playbook equally bars assuming they are Debt.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13), limitations applying to "Claims of any nature," and tax/IP/title all folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate regimes, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add an express hierarchy clause stating that the general limitations do not apply to these categories unless expressly stated.
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting creates exactly the hidden override the playbook prohibits. It would cap price, leakage, covenant and indemnity claims at the general levels.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. That means ASIC searches, PPSR searches, constitution and pre-emption waivers, board and shareholder approvals, and executed share transfers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add these as Completion deliverables.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is the Seller's own internal register, and DL 10 itself concedes that no Buyer verification has occurred. It is a supplied source, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as open. Do not assume unlimited liability, and do not assume they are resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep both on the open-issues list for separate negotiation.
- **Reason:** We have not agreed tax or IP terms, and folding them into a 20%/18-month regime would pre-empt that negotiation.

## Summary and Next Steps

| Status | Issues |
|---|---|
| **Reject and counter at playbook position** | 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 014, 015 |
| **Reject the characterisation and keep open** | 012, 013, 016 |
| **Accept as drafted** | None |

**Actions:**
1. Respond that no position is agreed or final. Flag that Wattlebridge has no record of principal-level settlement.
2. Escalate to Amelia Frost **only if** the team wishes to consider the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. Any authority must be written and must identify this draft. Do not trade these fallbacks without that authority.
3. Ask the Seller for a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter, as it is about six weeks stale. Specifically request:
   - Bluefen consent status and evidence on the cl 11.3 conditions
   - The Riverlark payout figure and draft releases
   - Ironquay payment evidence
   - The DD-006 investigation update
   - Payroll tax and on-cost treatment of the bonuses
   - Sandbar contract terms
4. Prepare a mark-up of cl 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5, Schedule 7 and the funds flow, reflecting the positions above.
